slides.title: Raise prices in 2027 where customers stay, hold them where customers are leaving

paragraphs.text: Raise prices in 2027 where customers stay, hold them where customers are leaving
Recommendation for Ravi Menon and the leadership team  |  Decision meeting, December 2026
Prepared only from the Palisade briefing pack. Its company, competitor and figures are synthetic benchmark data.
Figures marked “est.” are our calculations; the assumptions behind them are listed in Appendix A1.

slides.notes: Title. Deck answers the decision question in the briefing pack using only its data. All estimates are labelled; assumptions are listed in Appendix A1.

slides.title: Yes, raise prices in 2027: +10% in mid-market and up to contract caps in enterprise. Hold SMB prices until a Q1 test supports a rise

paragraphs.text: Yes, raise prices in 2027: +10% in mid-market and up to contract caps in enterprise. Hold SMB prices until a Q1 test supports a rise

Churn is rising almost only in the 2025 promotion cohort. Established SMB customers churn 2.1% a month (2.0% a year ago). The 2,100 promotion customers churn at an implied ~4.9% and make up ~56% of SMB churners. Mid-market (0.8%) and enterprise (0.2%) churn remains low.

The CFO is half right. Churn is not a broad price problem. But the promotion cohort is very price-sensitive: 52% of its churners cite price. And Inkwell’s $9 Starter plan has cut our SMB win rate from 51% to 38%.

A 12% rise on every plan is worth $7.6M gross in 2027, not $10.3M. 15% of mid-market ARR and 60% of enterprise ARR do not renew in 2027, and most enterprise contracts cap rises at 7%. In SMB, the rise nets anywhere from ~$1.2M to about zero once churn is counted.

Recommendation: raise prices segment by segment. +10% at mid-market renewal (the level tested in 2024). Enterprise: 7% where capped, 10% elsewhere. SMB list prices held in H1, with a Q1 test of +8% for established customers. Promotion-cohort prices frozen, plus an activation push. Est. $4.3M gross, $2.4–3.5M net.

The trade-off. On paper this is $0.3–1.8M less 2027 ARR than the CFO plan, but it avoids losing an extra ~320–640 SMB customers. NRR stays at ~112–113%. New customers still need to add ~$1.5–2.6M of ARR to reach +15%.
Decisions for December: approve the segmented plan, the SMB test and its go/no-go rule, and a single churn definition for board reporting.
Source: Palisade Docs briefing pack (synthetic data). Net figures are estimates; see Appendix A1.

slides.notes: Executive summary. Numbers: calc.py. CFO gross 7.57; CFO net 2.7-5.3; recommended gross 4.27, net 2.36-3.46.

slides.title: Rising churn is concentrated in the 2025 promotion cohort; churn among established customers is almost flat

paragraphs.text: Rising churn is concentrated in the 2025 promotion cohort; churn among established customers is almost flat
Monthly logo churn by customer group, %
of SMB ARR ($4.4M of $21.0M at full price)
of SMB customers who churned in H1 2026
So what: about 1.0 point of the 1.1-point rise in SMB churn comes from the promotion cohort. Without it, SMB churn would be 2.1%, close to last year’s 2.0%.
Mid-market churn has also edged up (0.6% to 0.8%). The pack does not explain why; it should be checked before renewals.

Source: Palisade Docs briefing pack (synthetic data), Table 1 and §6. Promotion-cohort churn is implied: (5,900 × 3.1% − 3,800 × 2.1%) ÷ 2,100 ≈ 4.9%, using mid-2026 customer counts as weights. The cohort joined Feb–Aug 2025, so it has no H1 2025 rate.

slides.title: Promotion customers left over price when the discount ended; weak activation explains only part of their churn

paragraphs.text: Promotion customers left over price when the discount ended; weak activation explains only part of their churn
Churners citing “price / found a cheaper option” as main reason, %
New customers sending ≥5 documents in month 1, %
SMB customers who send fewer than five documents in month 1 churn at about 3× the rate of those who send more.
Established customers are not more price-sensitive yet
Onboarding alone will not fix the cohort (est.)
They paid 50% less for six months. Most who left did so within two months of the discount ending, which for them was a 100% price step.
18% of non-promotion churners cite price, vs 19% of all SMB churners a year ago, even after Inkwell’s launch.
The activation gap accounts for ~0.8 of the cohort’s ~2.8-point excess churn (~30%). The rest coincides with the discount ending.
Implication: do not raise the promotion cohort’s price in 2027. A second price step within ~18 months would push out the customers onboarding is trying to save.
Source: Palisade Docs briefing pack (synthetic data), Table 2, §6 and §9. Exit-survey shares are of churners who answered. Activation split is our estimate; see Appendix A1.

slides.notes: Activation estimate: if low activators churn 3x others and non-promo (72% activated) churn 2.1%, then activated churn x=1.35%, low 4.0%; at 41% activation the promo cohort would churn ~2.9%, vs ~4.9% implied, so activation explains ~0.8 of ~2.8 pts excess (~30%).

slides.title: The CFO’s $10.3M is at most $7.6M in 2027 once renewal timing and enterprise caps are applied, before any churn

paragraphs.text: The CFO’s $10.3M is at most $7.6M in 2027 once renewal timing and enterprise caps are applied, before any churn
2027 ARR uplift from +12% on every plan at renewal, $M
Every dollar of ARR renews in 2027 and takes the full 12%.
60% of enterprise ARR is capped at 7% a year
The realistic gross figure is $2.8M (27%) lower, and churn has not yet been counted. Most of what remains comes from mid-market, not SMB.
Stress case (customers react twice as strongly): net $2.7M.

Source: Palisade Docs briefing pack (synthetic data), §4 and §8. We assume the capped share of enterprise ARR is the same in the 2027 renewal tranche. Churn responses are our estimates (pp. 7–8, Appendix A1).

slides.notes: 12% x 86.0 = 10.32. Less MM not renewing (15% x 41 x 12% = 0.74), Ent not renewing (60% x 24 x 12% = 1.73), Ent caps (9.6 x 60% x 5pts = 0.29) = 7.57 gross. Planning-case churn: SMB 1.27, MM 0.99 -> 5.30. Stress: SMB 2.54, MM 2.34 -> 2.68.

slides.title: In SMB, a 12% rise nets between +$1.2M and about zero, and costs an extra 320–640 customers

paragraphs.text: In SMB, a 12% rise nets between +$1.2M and about zero, and costs an extra 320–640 customers
2027 SMB ARR effect of +12% at renewal, $M (est.)
Premium over Inkwell Starter: 67% today, 87% after a 12% rise
Win rate already falling: down from 51% to 38% in SMB deals where Inkwell was considered.
The 2023 benchmark predates Inkwell. How price-sensitive established SMB customers are now is the pack’s main open question.
A permanent cost: in 2023, churn settled 0.1 point above where it started, so lost customers keep compounding.

Source: Palisade Docs briefing pack (synthetic data), §7–§8. Estimate: the 2023 response (+0.5 pt monthly churn for six months, +0.1 pt after) scaled to 12% removes ~5.4% of SMB customers over 12 months. Break-even for +12% is a loss of 10.7% of ARR.

slides.notes: SMB gross = 21.0 x 12% = 2.52. 2023 analog scaled to 12%: +0.75pt/month for 6 months and +0.15pt after -> 5.4% of SMB customers lost extra (~320) -> 1.27 ARR. Twice 2023: 10.8% (~640) -> 2.54. Break-even loss for +12% = 10.7% of ARR.

slides.title: In mid-market, +10% pays off unless it drives away over 9% of renewing ARR; the best evidence points to about 2%

paragraphs.text: In mid-market, +10% pays off unless it drives away over 9% of renewing ARR; the best evidence points to about 2%
Share of 2027 renewing mid-market ARR lost because of a +10% rise, %
gross: +10% on the 85% of ARR renewing
For scale: all mid-market churn today is ~9% of customers a year (0.8% a month). Losing 9% on price alone would mean the rise roughly doubles mid-market churn.
10% is the level we tested. 12% adds ~$0.7M gross but goes beyond the evidence, in the segment that carries 48% of ARR.
If accounts renewed at the new price in Q1 lose more than ~4% of their ARR (twice the planning case), pause further rises and review accounts of up to 200 seats before Q2 renewals.
The test covered new sign-ups, not renewals
Inkwell may reach accounts with 51–200 seats

Source: Palisade Docs briefing pack (synthetic data), §8–§9. Planning case: renewal losses equal the 2024 test’s relative conversion gap (23.1% vs 23.6%, 2.1%). The stress case of 5% is our assumption.

slides.notes: MM renewing ARR 2027 = 41.0 x 85% = 34.85. +10% = 3.49 gross. Break-even loss = 10/110 = 9.1%. Planning: 2.1% of renewing ARR lost (2024 test gap 23.1 vs 23.6) -> 0.81 -> net 2.67. Stress 5% -> 1.92 -> net 1.57.

Why C over A: A adds $0.3–1.8M more 2027 ARR on paper, almost all from SMB. That gain shrinks to nothing if SMB customers react twice as strongly as in 2023, and it costs customers in the one segment where a competitor is gaining ground.

slides.title: Recommended 2027 plan: raise prices where customers stay; hold and test where they are leaving

paragraphs.text: Recommended 2027 plan: raise prices where customers stay; hold and test where they are leaving
+10% on list price at renewal. Customer Success reviews accounts of up to 200 seats where Inkwell is present.
Renewals from Jan 2027 (85% of ARR), subject to notice terms
Pause if monthly churn exceeds 1.0% for a quarter
Up to the 7% cap on capped contracts; 10% target on the rest, negotiated account by account.
No change to multi-year terms in force
Hold list price in H1. Randomised test of +8% (the 2023 level) on half of Q1 renewals.
Test in Q1; decision by end of Q2; roll out in H2 if passed
Go only if extra churn is under 0.5 pt a month (the 2023 response)
No price rise in 2027. Activation outreach to low-usage accounts, measured against a holdout group.
Track cohort churn and usage monthly
Keep the $15 list price. No deep introductory discounts unless tied to activation.
Source: Palisade Docs briefing pack (synthetic data). The 2027 ARR effect is the run-rate once 2027 renewals complete; in-year revenue will be lower. SMB test design: see p. 13.

slides.notes: Enterprise: 9.6 renewing; 60% at 7% = 0.40, 40% at 10% = 0.38 -> 0.79. SMB H2 option: 16.6 x 8% x 50% = 0.66 gross.

slides.title: Even with the price rise, about $1.5–2.6M of the +15% ARR goal must come from new customers

paragraphs.text: Even with the price rise, about $1.5–2.6M of the +15% ARR goal must come from new customers
ARR growth needed in 2027 to reach +15% ($86.0M to $98.9M), $M (est.)
Price is the second-largest lever. Only option A, in its planning case, would close the gap without new customers.
Holding prices (option B) would leave ~$4.9M to new customers, about three times as much.
NRR stays well above the 100% floor (~112–113%).
The pack has no new-customer bookings or pipeline. Finance should confirm that $1.5–2.6M of new-customer ARR is realistic before December.
Base growth assumes trailing NRR holds; SMB NRR (94%) is the drag.
Stress case: price +2.4M, so new customers must add +2.6M.
Source: Palisade Docs briefing pack (synthetic data), §3 and Table 1. Today’s NRR is ARR-weighted from segment NRRs (21.0 × 94% + 41.0 × 112% + 24.0 × 118%) ÷ 86.0 ≈ 109%.

slides.notes: Target 98.9 = 86.0 x 1.15. Installed base at ARR-weighted NRR 109.3% adds 7.98. Price net 2.36-3.46. New logos needed 1.46-2.56.

slides.title: Fund onboarding, but plan on it cutting SMB churn by up to a third, not by half

paragraphs.text: Fund onboarding, but plan on it cutting SMB churn by up to a third, not by half
What onboarding can and cannot do
Can: lift activation. Only 41% of promotion customers sent five documents in month 1, against 72% of others, and low activators churn ~3× as often.
Cannot: halve SMB churn in two quarters. Even if the promotion cohort churned like everyone else, SMB churn would fall to 2.1%, not 1.55%.
Also: the cohort will shrink on its own, so blended SMB churn should fall even without action. Measure the programme against a holdout, not a before/after comparison.
Proposed targets for the Head of Customer Success
Raise the promotion cohort’s activation and cut its churn toward 2.1% a month; report against the holdout monthly
Make activation a condition of any future introductory discount
Source: Palisade Docs briefing pack (synthetic data), §6, §8–§10. SMB churn levels in the pack: 1.8% (before 2023 rise), 2.3% (2023 peak), 1.9% (after), 2.0% (H1 2025).

slides.notes: If the promo cohort churned at the non-promo rate (2.1%), SMB churn would be 2.1% = 32% lower than 3.1%. Halving = 1.55%, below any SMB level in the pack (1.8%-2.3%).

slides.title: Three checkpoints in 2027 let us stop or extend the rise before it hurts retention

paragraphs.text: Three checkpoints in 2027 let us stop or extend the rise before it hurts retention
Send renewal notices to mid-market and enterprise customers
Mid-market and enterprise renewals at the new prices
SMB +8% test on half of Q1 renewals
Activation programme starts, with a holdout
Read mid-market churn on accounts renewed at the new price
Early read of the SMB test
Set 2028 pricing: mid-market beyond 10%? SMB packaging against Inkwell?
Monthly logo churn above 1.0% for a quarter (0.8% today)
Pause further rises; review accounts of up to 200 seats
Test group churns 0.5 pt or more a month above control
No SMB list rise in H2; look at packaging against Inkwell instead
Churn not falling toward 2.1% by end of Q2
Stop investing in the cohort; focus onboarding on new customers

Thresholds are proposals derived from the break-even analysis (p. 8) and the 2023 SMB response (p. 7). The SMB test should be sized to detect a response twice the 2023 level, the point where an SMB rise stops paying.

slides.notes: Guardrails derived from break-even and 2023 analog. SMB test sized to detect a response twice the 2023 level (the level at which SMB pricing stops paying).

slides.title: Five decisions for the leadership team in December

paragraphs.text: Five decisions for the leadership team in December
Approve +10% on list price at renewal from January 2027, subject to notice periods, with Customer Success review of accounts of up to 200 seats.
Approve renewal pricing of up to the 7% cap on capped contracts and a 10% target on uncapped contracts.
Hold SMB list prices for H1 2027. Approve the Q1 +8% test on established customers and its go/no-go rule (extra churn under 0.5 pt a month).
Freeze the cohort’s prices for 2027. Fund the activation programme, measured against a holdout, with a target of ~2.1% monthly churn rather than “halving” SMB churn.
Adopt one churn definition: logo and revenue churn by segment, with the promotion cohort shown separately.
Open questions to close before the meeting
Finance: new-customer bookings outlook (we need $1.5–2.6M of new ARR) and the definition behind the board’s “1.4% → 2.3%” churn figure
Customer Success: why mid-market churn rose from 0.6% to 0.8%, and how much mid-market ARR sits in accounts of up to 200 seats
Legal: notice periods for January renewals, and whether capped enterprise contracts allow price rises during their term
Source: Palisade Docs briefing pack (synthetic data).

slides.title: Assumptions and calculations behind the estimates

paragraphs.text: Assumptions and calculations behind the estimates
Table 1; §6. Mid-2026 counts used as weights
Low activators churn 3× others. Non-promotion: 0.72x + 0.28 × 3x = 2.1%, so x = 1.35%. Cohort at 41% activation: ~2.9%, i.e. ~0.8 of ~2.8 pt
§8. Capped share assumed equal in the 2027 tranche
2023: +8% gave +0.5 pt a month for six months, +0.1 pt after. Scaled linearly: +12% loses 5.4% of customers (~320); stress case 2× (~640)
§8. Linear scaling and the 2× stress are our assumptions
Loss of renewing ARR = 2.1% per 10 pts of price (planning) or 5% (stress), applied to 34.85M × (1 + price)
2024 test: 23.1% vs 23.6% conversion; the test covered new sign-ups
None assumed; rises negotiated within caps
A rise of p pays off unless it loses more than p ÷ (1 + p) of the ARR it applies to: 9.1% at 10%, 10.7% at 12%
Target 86.0 × 1.15 = 98.9. Installed base at ARR-weighted NRR 109.3% adds 8.0; the rest comes from price and new customers
16.6M of established SMB ARR × 8% × half a year of renewals ≈ $0.7M gross ($1.3M full-year run-rate)
Source: Palisade Docs briefing pack (synthetic data). All figures are reproducible from the pack; ARR effects are run-rate at the end of 2027.

slides.notes: Assumptions and calculations; all reproducible in work/calc.py.

slides.title: Data issues to resolve: the board’s churn figure cannot be reproduced from segment data

paragraphs.text: Data issues to resolve: the board’s churn figure cannot be reproduced from segment data
Mid-market churn rise. It rose from 0.6% to 0.8% with no explanation in the pack. It needs checking before renewal notices go out.
Exit-survey coverage. Shares cover respondents only. As a check, mixing promotion and other churners gives ~37% citing price, vs 34% reported, which is broadly consistent.
Renewal response. The only mid-market test covered new sign-ups (uncertainty 3).
New-customer bookings. These are not in the pack, so the +15% bridge cannot be fully tested.
Contract terms. Notice periods, and whether capped contracts allow rises during their term.

Neither weighting matches the dashboard, and a single blended number hides the story: the rise is concentrated in one cohort in one segment. We recommend reporting logo and revenue churn by segment, with the promotion cohort shown separately.
Source: Palisade Docs briefing pack (synthetic data), Table 1, Table 2, §10–§11. Weighted averages use mid-2026 customer counts and ARR for both periods.
